clue.text: Cartoon character frames mischievous graph

indicators.note: to frame something is to surround it, so the cartoon name goes around the other piece

parts.note: Bart Simpson, the cartoon boy
arch means playfully mischievous, as in an arch smile

explanation.surface: A cartoon boy is seen holding up some cheeky diagram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mischievous' looks like a description of the cartoon character, but it supplies its own piece, as in an arch grin.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar chart is a diagram showing quantities as columns of differing heights, a kind of graph.

clue.text: Benefit when pinching fool's instrument

indicators.note: pinching means squeezing something between, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a boon is a benefit or blessing
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A perk arrives when a joker swipes a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The bassoon is a large double-reed woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Monarch initially supporting genuine kingdom

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece sits beneath, so it comes after the other

parts.note: real means genuine

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A king is first propping up an authentic kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Casino big shots — they may rock the boat!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: gamblers who stake large sums
second meaning: tall waves that roll a vessel

explanation.walkthrough: 'rock the boat' usually means cause trouble; here it is literal, big waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamblers placing huge bets are known by this phrase, and large rolling sea swells could be described the same way.

clue.text: Mike taken in by thin-sounding treatment

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so the letter goes within the following word

parts.note: reedy describes a high, thin voice
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Mike is fooled by a feeble-sounding cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a cure or treatment for an illness.

clue.text: Mark's small vehicle

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a car is a road vehicle

explanation.surface: Somebody called Mark owns a little car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name owning something; it is the definition, and the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the blemish left on skin after a wound heals, a lasting mark.

clue.text: Greek character not in favour of wine from Italy

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
anti means opposed to

explanation.surface: A Greek man refuses an Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from the Tuscany region.

clue.text: Whistleblower is on top of computing overhaul

indicators.note: in a down answer being on top means coming first, above the other piece

parts.note: a referee blows a whistle
IT, information technology, is computing

explanation.surface: A leaker of secrets is busy with a computer revamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistleblower' suggests an informant; here it is the referee.
explanation.definitionFit: To refit a ship or building is to repair and re-equip it, an overhaul.

clue.text: Young ladies returning, having adopted Northern jargon

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the reversed word takes the abbreviation inside it
returning says the word for young women is read backwards

parts.note: gals is informal for young women
N is the compass abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: Girls coming home have picked up northern dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns GALS into SLAG, and N then goes inside it: SLA-N-G.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal vocabulary used by a particular group, a sort of jargon.

clue.text: Mother with wooden dog

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
wooden, of a manner, means stiff and awkward

explanation.surface: A mother is out with a toy dog carved from wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastiff is a large, powerful breed of guard dog.

clue.text: Award two silver medals maybe for a brief period?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: share the runner-up place in a tie

explanation.walkthrough: Split second literally describes dividing second place between two competitors.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a tiny fraction of time, and also, read literally, a tie for runner-up.

clue.text: Resistance unit primarily orders heavy machinery

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: An electrical unit mostly governs the purchase of heavy plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The ohm is the SI measure of electrical resistance, named after Georg Ohm.

clue.text: Mars alien appears after communist plot

indicators.note: appears after says the alien comes at the end, following the other pieces

parts.note: red is a common byword for a communist
a plan is a scheme or plot
E.T. is the film alien

explanation.surface: A Martian shows up after a Soviet conspiracy is hatched.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars is nicknamed this because its iron-oxide dust gives the planet a rusty colour.

clue.text: Require extremely large and pointy implement

parts.note: to require is to need

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so take the outermost letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone insists they must have a big, sharp tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A needle is a slender sewing tool with a sharp tip, plainly pointed.

clue.text: Overshadow some movie clips eventually

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Film excerpts end up stealing the limelight from the main feature.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse a rival is to outshine them so they are overlooked, a figurative sense from astronomy.

clue.text: High priest's signifier of rank

indicators.note: high here means intoxicated, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A senior cleric's badge of office is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High priest' reads as one title, but 'High' is the anagram signal for PRIEST, and the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe on a uniform sleeve marks a soldier's grade, as with a sergeant's stripes.

clue.text: Serious art seen to become silly

indicators.note: becoming silly means going wild, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sober art is viewed as turning frivolous.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and grave in intention, the opposite of frivolous.

clue.text: Very advanced phone ultimately beset by snag

indicators.note: beset means surrounded, so the letter sits inside the other word

parts.note: a hitch is a snag or problem

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so take the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cutting-edge phone ends up plagued by a glitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-tech means using the most sophisticated modern technology.

clue.text: Wine lover disturbed carnivore

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A wine enthusiast is upset by a predatory animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The wolverine is a fierce flesh-eating mammal of the weasel family.

clue.text: Compose beginning of wedding ceremony

indicators.note: beginning of means take the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: Someone drafts the opening of a marriage service.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose a letter or music is to write it.

clue.text: Tune from duo without piano

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the musical letter is taken away

parts.note: a duo is a pair
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A musical pair plays a melody with no keyboard accompaniment.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a simple melody, a song or tune.

clue.text: Straighten a queue, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as is said, so the answer sounds like the words

parts.note: a queue is a line, giving 'a line'

explanation.surface: Someone is told to tidy up a waiting line.
explanation.definitionFit: To align things is to bring them into a straight row.

clue.text: What a has-been may say is a deadlock?

indicators.note: may say means spoken aloud, so the answer is how the confession sounds

parts.note: a washed-up person might confess to being out of date, using the French word for faded fashion

explanation.surface: A faded star's admission is offered as the name for a stalemate.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, I'M PASSÉ (I am out of date) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a situation where no progress is possible, a stalemate.

clue.text: Offer a view on pie mixture

indicators.note: a mixture stirs things together, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gives their opinion about a pie filling.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state one's opinion, a formal verb for giving a view.

clue.text: Occasion is cut short — that's not odd!

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is removed

parts.note: an event is an occasion

explanation.surface: An occasion ended early, which is hardly strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not odd' seems to mean unsurprising; it is the number sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An even number divides by two, the opposite of an odd one.

clue.text: Intelligence to capture terrible hound in murder mystery

indicators.note: capturing something holds it inside, so the scrambled letters go within the other word

parts.note: wit means intelligence or sharpness of mind

indicators.note: terrible means badly done, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Detective brains are needed to catch a dreadful hound, as in a Baskervilles crime story.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Sherlock Holmes and the Hound of the Baskervilles, which fits the definition neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunit is a detective story built around discovering the killer.
